en_title: Entrepreneur Talk: with a creative, light and motivating touch, to inspire anyone thinking of starting a business — and also to spark some good laughs and deep reflections 😉
en_excerpt: Nail designer Cristiane Lima talks about restarting her career in Ireland, her fear of beginning again and the advice she would give new entrepreneurs.
en_meta_description: A warm, honest chat with nail designer Cristiane Lima about rebuilding her business abroad and what it really takes to be an entrepreneur.
en_content:
1. Who are you?

My name is Cristiane Lima, I am a nail designer, manicurist and pedicurist. My journey in the world of nails began in 2015, in Brazil, when I decided to turn my passion for beauty into a profession.

https://www.instagram.com/espacocris.nails/

It was in Brazil that I completed my first qualification in the field and began building my professional experience. From the start, I always saw the world of nails as something far beyond aesthetics. To me, every appointment represents self-esteem, care, confidence and a connection with each client.

Over these 10 years of my journey, I have kept evolving, learning new techniques and understanding more and more the importance of delivering work with excellence, attention to detail and professionalism.

In 2022, I arrived in Portugal and started seeing a few clients, trying to restart my career in a new country. But at that moment I faced insecurities, fear and the natural challenges of starting from scratch far from home. In the end I gave up for a while, but the passion for my profession never stopped existing inside me.

Today, living in Ireland, I have decided to come back with everything I have and start again in an even stronger and more professional way. Here in Ireland, I also took a new qualification to update my techniques, sharpen my knowledge and offer an ever more qualified service.

And my journey does not stop here: soon I will take another qualification in Portugal, because I believe that a professional who strives for excellence never stops evolving. I want to keep growing, learning and keeping up with new trends and techniques so that I always deliver the best for my clients.

My goal is to build work that is seen, recognised and admired for its professionalism, quality and care in every detail — not only for my own personal growth, but above all to provide a special experience for every woman who sits in my chair.

2. When did you realise you wanted to become an entrepreneur, and how did you choose this niche?

I realised I wanted to become an entrepreneur when I understood that I could build something of my own, with my own identity, my own quality standards and my own way of serving people. I chose the beauty niche because I have always enjoyed turning small details into self-esteem.

The world of nails enchanted me because it brings together technique, creativity, care and connection with people. Every appointment is an opportunity to make someone feel more beautiful, confident and happy.

3. What was your biggest fear or challenge in this process?

My biggest challenge was believing that I could start over in another country. Leaving your comfort zone, facing your insecurities and starting again takes a lot of courage. But I learned that every difficult phase is also part of building our story.

4. What was the biggest scrape on your entrepreneurial journey that you now laugh about? 😂

One of the biggest scrapes was realising that being an entrepreneur is not just doing beautiful nails. There is the diary, materials, promotion, customer service, organisation, chasing payments and still keeping your emotions in balance. Today I laugh, but at the beginning I nearly went mad trying to be manicurist, social media manager, finance department and receptionist all at once. 😂

5. If you did not have this business, which other niche would you try?

I would probably go into something related to fashion, aesthetics or creative communication. I have always enjoyed everything that involves beauty, self-esteem and connecting with people.

6. What is your life motto?

“Do everything with love, dedication and excellence, because the details speak for you.”

7. What does success mean to you today?

To me, success is balance. It is having financial results, professional recognition, freedom and, above all, knowing that my work has a positive impact on people's lives.

8. Which small everyday victory gives you that quiet happiness?

When a client looks at the final result and smiles spontaneously. It is a simple detail, but it reminds me every day why I chose this profession.

9. Which habit or mindset shift transformed your business?

Understanding that I needed to value myself professionally. When I started to see my work more seriously, invest in knowledge and stop being afraid to charge what I am worth, everything began to change.

10. What do you think could be improved in your business?

I always believe I can improve my digital presence, my organisation and the client experience. Being an entrepreneur means being in constant evolution.

11. What honest advice would you give to someone who wants to become an entrepreneur?

Do not romanticise the journey. Being an entrepreneur is beautiful, but it is also tiring, and it demands discipline, consistency and a lot of patience. Not every day will be motivating, but carrying on even on the hard days makes all the difference.
